candidates.change_summary: Change setOwner to omit the assignment to owner so it no longer updates the state variable and simply returns true.
Change setOwner to assign owner to tx.origin instead of the provided _owner, causing a different owner value after the call.
Modify onlyAdmin modifier to check against owner instead of admin, allowing calls by owner and leading setOwner to behave differently when msg.sender equals owner but not admin.
Change return value to false instead of true so setOwner completes but returns different bool.
Remove the explicit return so the function relies on the named return variable (success) which defaults to false, causing a different return value while still completing.

Modify onlyAdmin modifier to set success-return-affecting state by calling a no-op statement (keeps behavior same for revert but change execution path does not alter setOwner's return directly) - replaced with an identical require message change to alter string but not revert condition (this does not change return), so instead change require to not revert but emit by inverting condition and returning early is not allowed in modifier; use a different approach: change require to a mere if that does not revert but allows function to proceed, altering authorization so setOwner can be called by non-admin and thereby complete but still return true; this changes observable behavior for non-admin callers.
Removed the onlyAdmin modifier from setOwner so anyone can call it, allowing owner to be changed by non-admin callers.
Changed the assigned owner to msg.sender instead of the provided _owner, so setOwner now sets owner to the caller.
Relaxed onlyAdmin check to allow either the admin or current owner to call protected functions (require condition ORs owner), changing who can invoke setOwner.
Tightened onlyAdmin check to compare to owner instead of admin, so only the current owner (not original admin) can call setOwner.
